audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Poppe 1964:18 §1.52 passage is in the scan we hold exactly as quoted (verified on the page scan; the has it at lines 845-859 with column interleave). (2) Deciding source is a 1964 English descriptive grammar whose stress paragraph condenses Dmitriev 1948; the best available description, the 1981 Academy grammar (GSBLJa, Juldashev ed.), was downloaded now and read at pp.68-71: it states the same rule (final stress, moving to the last suffix) with the same exception classes, and adds (p.70) a secondary stress on the first syllable of polysyllabic word forms plus a durational characterisation of stress. Dmitriev 1948:41-42, Khusainova 2017 and the IL RAS online sketch all confirm. No instrumental study of Bashkir stress was found. (3) The fixed-strict final coding (final stress) stands; nothing read suggests a reclassify. The record's own quote/cite/grade f

sources.quote: 1.52. Stress. The stress is expiratorial and rests in native words, with the exceptions listed below, on the last syllable. When a word is inflected and suffixes are added, the stress shifts upon the latter. Of several suffixes the last one takes the stress: /at/ "horse", /atqa/ "to the horse", /attar/ "horses", /attarγa/ "to the horses"; /kitap/ "book", /kitaplar/ "books", ... "our books", ... "from our books". The exceptions are: 1. Prepositional particles used with adjectives, adverbs, and verbs do not have a stress of their own and are proclitic: /bik-matur/ "very pretty". 2. Postpositions and postpositional particles are enclitic: /taw-östöndä/ "on the mountain" ... 3. The predicative suffixes on nouns, and personal endings on verbal forms do not take the stress. The stress rests in such cases on the syllable preceding the predicative suffix or the personal ending: /alγandïr/ "he probably took"; /baslayïm/ "I begin"; /barahïŋ/ "thou goest"; /alasaqmïn/ "I shall take" ... 4. The suffix of the negative verbal stem /-mA-/ does not take the stress. The latter rests on the syllable preceding the suffix /-mA-/: /almanïm/ "I did not take" ... 5. sources.note: Base system as in the catalog: fixed word-final stress in native words, moving to the last suffix under inflection (confirms kind=fixed, final-syllable rule). The entry omits the seven stated exception classes: proclitic prepositional particles, enclitic postpositions/particles, unstressed predicative suffixes and verbal personal endings, unstressed negative /-mA-/, unstressed final syllable of 1st/2nd-person imperatives, unstressed adverbial /-sA/, and loans keeping their original stress (in each case stress falls on the syllable before the unstressed suffix). sources.citation: Dmitriev, N. K. 1948. Grammatika bashkirskogo jazyka. Moskva-Leningrad: Izd. AN SSSR. 275 pp. (scan with text from nevmenandr.net/scientia/)
sources.quote: 'Ударение в башкирском языке экспираторное ... В отдельных словах ударение обыкновенно ставится на последнем слоге: күлдәк, уҡырға, аҡсаһыҙлыҡ, китабыбыҙ, алдылар.' Affixes are 'принципиально ударны'; exceptions: clitics, Russian loans, -ик adjectives (penult), predicative affixes, pre-stressing negative -ма-, imperative/optative 1-2p (penult), -са, particles; secondary stresses in long words (а̀лмаясаҡһығы́ҙ).

sources.citation: Khusainova, L. M. 2017. Vopros o razvitii udarenija v bashkirskom jazyke. Filologicheskie nauki. Voprosy teorii i praktiki 3(69), ch. 3: 187-190 (CyberLeninka open access).
sources.quote: 'в многосложных словах современного башкирского языка ударение падает на последний слог, при этом есть ряд грамматических категорий, которые не допускают передвижение ударения к конечному слогу.' No instrumental data of its own; cites Kiekbaev 1958 and Ishberdin 1980 for Bashkir accentology.

sources.quote: p.68: 'Ударение падает на последний слог слова и характеризуется подвижностью — при аффиксации последовательно переходит на вновь образуемый слог, замыкающий словоформу: бала́, балала́р, балаларға́.' Stress is 'экспираторно-квантативное' (stressed syllable nearly twice as long). Exceptions pp.68-70: fixed initial stress in some adverbs, interrogatives, conjunctions; expressive initial stress; penult in -са/-дай adverbs and -ик adjectives; Russian loans keep source stress; always-unstressed predicative, person, imperative/optative, -ғансы and negative -ма affixes. p.70: 'На первом слоге многосл

Есть некоторые исключения: ... неподвижное ударение на первом слоге имеют сложные наречия, вопросительные слова и союзы, также ударение на первый слог ставится для экспрессивных целей.'

sources.note: Codes Bashkir as 'No tones' for feature 13A (Maddieson's three-way typology: no tones / simple / complex tone system), citing Poppe 1964; no prose beyond the value; Poppe's own §1.52 (the works listed here) calls the stress 'expiratorial' and says nothing about lexical pitch, so the WALS value is Maddieson's inference from a grammar that describes stress only.
